note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 2391 / 出力 1588 トークン

data.interpretation: The operator wants road rules to be obeyed, measured by road-rule violations (release deadline overruns and blocking_guard evictions), pushed as low as possible. The stated target is a count of violations. That count is a proxy for the real aim, which is orderly, unobstructed road use. It can be lowered in ways that do not serve that aim: loosening or removing the rules so fewer events count as violations, or making robots move or deliver less.

options.label: Minimize road violations, watching that road use and service do not get worse

goals.text: Reduce the number of road-rule violations (release overruns and blocking_guard evictions).
Watch that total time robots spend blocked does not grow, so fewer violations reflects better road use and not just fewer counted events.
Watch that town-wide on-time deliveries do not fall, so violations are not cut by making robots do less.
Watch that orders left undelivered at period end do not increase.

options.note: Follows the KPI wording literally, with watch goals that catch the two main ways the count can be gamed. No numeric guards are set because baseline values are not yet known. Once the current seed has been measured, the operator may want hard guards such as on_time_deliveries >= baseline.

options.label: Minimize actual obstruction, keeping the violation count as a watch

goals.text: Reduce total time robots are blocked by stopped robots, which is the harm the road rules exist to prevent.
Watch that road-rule violations do not increase.
Watch that town-wide on-time deliveries do not fall.

options.note: Reads 'make sure the road rules are kept' as aimed at the purpose of the rules (unobstructed roads). Choosing this means a change that cuts blocking but leaves the violation count flat would still count as an improvement.

concerns: road_violations is defined by the rules themselves. A ROAD_USE amendment that lengthens release deadlines or weakens or removes blocking_guard would lower the count without making robots behave better. The operator should decide whether loosening the rules counts as 'keeping' them, or whether only stricter or equal rules are acceptable.

Violations can also be reduced by having robots travel or deliver less, for example through more conservative operating modes. This would hurt service. Option 1 only watches for this; the operator may want hard guards on on_time_deliveries or unfinished once a baseline is measured.

The KPI says 'as much as possible' with no limit on what may be traded away. If cutting violations conflicts with on-time delivery or fairness between companies, the operator needs to say how much service loss, if any, is acceptable.
